title: Accessible color-mapped cost heatmap & localized numeric scrubber for Dashboards
creator: Marisol Ortega
description:
Problem: The current cost heatmap and time-series scrubber in the Dashboards view relies on subtle color gradients and a visual-only hover scrubber. This causes two accessibility issues: 1) color-contrast fails WCAG thresholds for some palette extremes and certain user themes (high contrast / dim); 2) keyboard and screen-reader users cannot reliably navigate or receive context while scrubbing time ranges, and localized number formatting is not consistently exposed to assistive tech.

Objective: Deliver a design that: (a) remaps heatmap tokens to contrast-safe, color-blind-friendly palette tokens with clear semantic token names for engineering; (b) introduces a keyboard-accessible numeric scrubber control for the cost time-series that announces locale-aware values and unit suffixes; (c) ensures RTL layout and number formatting parity; (d) provides an implementation-ready spec and prototype for engineering and QA.

Scope: Focused on the Cost heatmap card and the primary time-series scrubber used in Dashboard charts and Rollouts cost comparisons. Not in scope: embedding explorer and legacy Cost Explorer page (tracked separately).

Stakeholders: PM: Lena Schultz; Eng owners: Kai Nguyen (frontend), Priya Rao (runtime/metrics); Accessibility SME: Omar Hassan; QA: Amina Wallace.

Deliverables: Figma prototype with keyboard interactions, annotated token mapping doc, acceptance criteria, implementation notes for aria/live-region behavior, and a small a11y test checklist (NVDA, VoiceOver, VoiceOver on iOS, TalkBack).
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap uses a named semantic token set where every token pair meets at least AA contrast ratio for both light and dark themes (WCAG 2.1 4.5:1 for body text-equivalent elements and 3:1 for large targets where applicable)
Color palette includes a color-blind-safe variant and fallback to system high-contrast mode. Engineering can switch palette via token flag.

Keyboard scrubber: focusable control that responds to Left/Right (step), PageUp/PageDown (coarse), Home/End (start/end) and uses aria-live region to announce localized numeric values and units on change.
Numbers announced and visually displayed use Intl.NumberFormat with user's locale and timezone; engineering has locale examples (en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, ar-SA) in the spec.
RTL: layout flips correctly and numeric announcements maintain LTR numeric ordering while UI direction is RTL; design shows alignment and icon mirroring.
Prototype demonstrates both mouse and full keyboard workflows and includes a screen-reader narration script for testing.
Design tokens and mapping spreadsheet delivered to ENG-4021 with migration notes and suggested rollout plan (canary -> 50% -> full).
QA passes: axe automated checks (no new violations), manual checks with NVDA/VoiceOver for the scrubber announcements and focus order, and color contrast tests across themes.
implementation_notes: Expose semantic tokens: --cost-heatmap-bg-0 .. --cost-heatmap-bg-5 and --cost-heatmap-accent; match names in tokens spreadsheet.
Provide CSS variables for high-contrast user-agent override and a boolean token 'prefers-high-contrast' handled by runtime.

Scrubber should be implemented as a composite control: role='slider' for the time index with aria-valuetext reflecting localized value + unit, plus a visually-hidden live region for progressive announcements when dragging.
Use Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { maximumFractionDigits: 2, notation: 'compact' }) for visual and audible displays; include explicit decimals when step changes are fractional.
Ensure keyboard focus order: chart legend -> scrubber -> chart area -> cost-card action menu. Add focus-visible styles that meet contrast requirements.
Eng to add E2E test harness with voiceover script using macOS accessibility automation and an axe snapshot in CI for chart components.
Rollout plan: feature flag 'a11y_cost_heatmap_v2' and staged CSS token swap; coordinate with runtime to avoid flashing token changes for long-lived charts.
